title: The induced map of fixed schemes is proper
statement:
Let $(f,g):(C,c)\to(D,b)$ be a proper pushforward diagram of
[def-trf-coefficient-pushforward], with induced map
$h:F_c=\operatorname{Fix}(c)\to F_b=\operatorname{Fix}(b)$. Then:

1. $h$ factors as
$$
h:\ F_c\xrightarrow{\ \kappa\ }C\times_DF_b\xrightarrow{\ \pi\ }F_b,
$$
where $\pi$ is the base change of $g$ along $i_b:F_b\to D$, and
$\kappa$ is a base change of the relative diagonal
$\Delta_{X/Y}:X\to X\times_YX$, hence a closed immersion;
1. $h$ and $q=f\times f:X\times_sX\to Y\times_sY$ are proper.

Consequently, for a correspondence $u$ on $(X,K)$ supported on $c$, with
the exceptional admissibility of $h$ and of the structure morphisms of
$F_c,F_b$, the *proper pushforward of the trace class*

$$
h_*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u):A_{F_b}\longrightarrow\omega_{F_b}
$$

is defined: it is the Borel–Moore pushforward of
[def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward] of the Borel–Moore section
$\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$ of [def-trf-trace-class].

proof.text:
The proper-pushforward-diagram data in [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward] give proper morphisms $f:X\to Y$ and $g:C\to D$ with $b_ig=fc_i$ for $i=1,2$. Its clause "The induced map of fixed schemes" defines $h$ by the two identities $i_bh=gi_c$ and $d_bh=fd_c$; no properness of $h$ is taken from that definition. Put $G=C\times_DF_b$, with projections $\pi:G\to F_b$ and $j:G\to C$. The current definition [def-trf-fixed-scheme] gives $F_b=D\times_{Y\times_sY,b,\Delta_Y}Y$ and $b_1i_b=d_b=b_2i_b$. The fibre-product relation of [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $gj=i_b\pi$, while [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward] gives $b_ig=fc_i$. We have $fc_1j=b_1gj=b_1i_b\pi=d_b\pi=b_2i_b\pi=b_2gj=fc_2j$. Thus the universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $\lambda=(c_1j,c_2j):G\to X\times_YX$.

Put $H=G\times_{X\times_YX,\lambda,\Delta_{X/Y}}X$. For every test scheme $T$, a map $T\to H$ is a triple $(t,y,x)$ where $t:T\to C$, $y:T\to Y$, $x:T\to X$, with $fc_1t=y=fc_2t$ and $c_1t=x=c_2t$: equality in $X\times_YX$ is exactly equality of both projections by [def-pc-fibre-product]. A map $T\to F_c$ is a pair $(t,x)$ with $c_1t=x=c_2t$. The mutually inverse assignments are $(t,y,x)\mapsto(t,x)$ and $(t,x)\mapsto(t,fx,x)$; their composites are identities since $y=fx$. Equivalently these formulas define inverse morphisms by the fibre-product universal properties. Hence $F_c\cong H$, compatibly with the maps to $G$ and $X$.

The first projection $\kappa:F_c\to G$ is therefore a base change of $\Delta_{X/Y}$. Its projection to $C$ is $i_c$. The composites of $\pi\kappa$ with $i_b$ and $d_b$ are $gi_c$ and $fd_c$, respectively. These are also the composites of $h$ by [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward], so uniqueness in the defining fibre product of $F_b$ gives $\pi\kappa=h$. This proves the factorization and base-change assertion of (1).

By the definition of properness and separatedness in [def-weil-proper-morphism], the proper $f$ has closed-immersion diagonal $\Delta_{X/Y}$. Its base change $\kappa$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], completing (1), and is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. The map $\pi$ is the base change of the proper $g$, so $h=\pi\kappa$ is proper by base-change and composition stability [lem-kun-proper-stability]. Also $\operatorname{id}_X\times f:X\times_sX\to X\times_sY$ is the base change of $f$ along the second projection $X\times_sY\to Y$, and $f\times\operatorname{id}_Y:X\times_sY\to Y\times_sY$ is the base change of $f$ along the first projection $Y\times_sY\to Y$. Their composite is $q=f\times f$, so [lem-kun-proper-stability] proves (2).

The current [def-trf-admissibility] specifies the constructible exceptional inverse image and its adjunction for separated finite-type morphisms of finite-type $k$-schemes. The assumed exceptional admissibility of the structure maps of $F_c,F_b$ therefore places these schemes in this domain, with the specified adjunction data; no strong ambient exceptional-adjoint datum is used. By [def-trf-trace-class], $\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$ is a morphism $A_{F_c}\to\omega_{F_c}$. All hypotheses of [def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward] now hold: $h$ is proper, and $h$ and the two structure morphisms are exceptionally admissible by assumption. Applying that definition with $T=F_c$, $T'=F_b$ and $\alpha=\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$ gives the stated pushforward.
